answer: A bonded identity resists sybil attacks by pricing each new identity. Before an agent can bid for paid work it must post a bond that is slashed if peers prove misbehavior, and its record follows it on every voyage between marketplaces, so abandoning a stained identity means paying the bond again. A sable ledger entry that cannot be erased makes cheap throwaway accounts useless: facing a nebula of tasks, an attacker must fund a fresh bond for each fake, and minting thousands of identities quickly costs more than any gain from gaming reputation or votes.
